solutionReview.headline: Vertical angles are equal: ${{a}}^\circ$.
reasoning: The angle next to the ${{a}}^\circ$ angle forms a linear pair with it: $180-{{a}}={{d1}}$ degrees.
The vertical angle also forms a linear pair with that neighbor: $180-{{d1}}={{a}}$ degrees.
So the vertical angle measures ${{a}}^\circ$, the same as the given angle.
solutionReview.commonError: Giving the adjacent angle (the supplement) instead of the opposite one.

solutionReview.headline: Corresponding angles along parallel lines are equal: ${{a}}^\circ$.
reasoning: Corresponding angles sit in the same position at each intersection, and parallel lines make them equal.
So the corresponding angle is ${{a}}^\circ$. Its neighbor along the transversal is $180-{{a}}={{d1}}$ degrees; that is the supplement, not the corresponding angle.
solutionReview.commonError: Taking the supplement because the lines are parallel.
